steps.name: Define significant gene set from DESeq2 results
steps.context: de_results.csv is a DESeq2 output table (gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2fc-related SE/stat, p-value, padj columns) for the 6 treated (AD lesional) vs 6 control contrast on 12000 genes. This step only filters/prepares gene lists; it does not re-run DESeq2.
steps.question: Which genes in the treated (AD lesional) vs control DESeq2 contrast pass standard significance thresholds (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1), and what is the full background gene universe for enrichment testing?
constraints: Use padj (BH-adjusted p-value) column, not raw p-value, for significance filtering
Use the actual column names present in de_results.csv (gene, log2_fold_change, padj or equivalent) rather than assuming exact names — inspect the header first
Background must be all genes with a non-missing test result in de_results.csv, not the raw counts.csv gene list, since DESeq2 independent filtering may have set some padj to NA
acceptance_criteria: Produces a significant-gene list (gene symbols) filtered from de_results.csv on adjusted p-value < 0.05 and |log2_fold_change| > 1
Reports the count of significant genes (up- and down-regulated separately) and flags if the list is empty or very small (<10 genes), which would make ORA unreliable
Produces a background/universe gene list = all 12000 genes tested in de_results.csv (non-NA padj), for use as the ORA background
Output files are plain gene-symbol lists (CSV/TXT) usable by clusterProfiler

steps.name: GO Biological Process over-representation analysis (ORA)
steps.context: Human (Homo sapiens, taxon 9606) skin RNA-seq. A GO Biological Process gene-set reference for human is available at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-go-human/2026.1/c5.go.bp.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt (7,538 GOBP_* sets, HGNC symbols) for use as the GMT-based cross-check; org.Hs.eg.db/GO.db provide the primary clusterProfiler annotation source. Do not use the mouse or rat GO/pathway files present in the reference store — organism must stay human throughout.
steps.question: Which Gene Ontology Biological Process terms are significantly over-represented among the genes significant in the treated (AD lesional) vs control contrast, relative to the full tested gene background?
constraints: Gene symbols in de_results.csv must be matched to org.Hs.eg.db SYMBOL keytype (or mapped to ENTREZID) before running enrichGO — verify mapping rate and report genes that fail to map
Use the background gene list from T1S1 (universe argument), not clusterProfiler's default whole-genome background, since the assay only measured ~12000 genes
State explicitly that GO's nested hierarchy means top hits will be correlated/overlapping processes, not independent discoveries, even after simplify()
acceptance_criteria: Runs hypergeometric ORA (clusterProfiler::enrichGO, ont='BP') on the significant gene list from T1S1 against the full background gene list from T1S1, using org.Hs.eg.db for human gene symbol-to-GO mapping
Reports BH-adjusted p-values (qvalue) for each enriched GO BP term at a standard significance cutoff (padj < 0.05)

Cross-checks the top enriched terms against the MSigDB human GO-BP gene set collection (c5.go.bp.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt) via a second ORA (e.g. clusterProfiler::enricher or gseapy) as an independent gene-set source, and reports concordance/discordance between the two annotation sources
Applies GO term redundancy reduction (e.g. clusterProfiler::simplify or equivalent semantic-similarity collapsing) so nested parent/child BP terms are not reported as independent findings
Outputs a ranked table of significant GO BP terms (term name, GO ID, gene ratio, background ratio, adjusted p-value, enriched genes) and a dot/bar plot of top terms
If T1S1 reports an empty or very small (<10 gene) significant list, this step must report that ORA is underpowered/not performed rather than force a run on a trivial gene set

plan.title: GO BP over-representation in AD lesional vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The DESeq2 results table (de_results.csv, 12000 genes x 8 columns) already contains the treated (AD lesional) vs control contrast statistics (log2FC, adjusted p-value), so no re-computation of differential expression is needed. The plan (1) defines the significant gene list from the existing DESeq2 results using standard thresholds, using the full 12000-gene table as the background/universe, (2) runs GO Biological Process over-representation analysis (ORA, hypergeometric test) against that gene list using clusterProfiler with org.Hs.eg.db for human gene ID mapping, cross-checked against the MSigDB human GO-BP GMT as an independent gene-set source, and (3) collapses redundant/nested GO terms (a known property of the GO hierarchy) before reporting so the output is not dominated by highly overlapping parent/child terms. All steps operate on the human (Homo sapiens, taxon 9606) skin dataset already provided; no external cohorts are required for this question.
